- You implemented SAML assertion signature verification for Fernhill's Okta — assertion-level signatures, SHA-256+ only, per-tenant IdP certificates, replay cache — and opened PR #418 for Maya's review [2].
- You killed the flaky `test_acs_rejects_expired_assertion` by freezing time instead of sleeping, converted the two other sleep-based tests, and brought `kestrel/auth` to clean ruff 0.8 + mypy — missing Issuer/Subject now yields 401 instead of a 500 [1].

- You parked that cleanup on branch `daniel/auth-cleanup` as PR #423, deliberately leaving #418 untouched [1].

## What changed

- Maya approved and merged #418 last night; it ships with the staging deploy — signature validation is on staging ahead of the Wed EOD deadline for Fernhill [3][1].
- Tom requested changes on #423: he wants the module move split from the lint fixes into two PRs, since the 1,900-line diff hides the real changes; he said he'd approve both today [4].

## What is still open

- The Fernhill end-to-end SSO walkthrough on staging is Thursday 10:00 NY time against their Okta tenant; Priya runs the demo, you only need to be on the call [1].
- Split #423 into two PRs as Tom asked and get them approved today [4].
- Your queued task: move the assertion-ID replay cache to Redis so replay protection holds across the 3 API pods — it's an in-process TTLCache today [1].
